questions.stem: Which of the following errors will NOT affect the trial balance?
questions.explanation: Compensating errors involve multiple errors that cancel each other out, so they do not affect the trial balance.

distractorRationale.a: Errors of omission may not affect the balance if both debit and credit are omitted.
distractorRationale.b: Errors of commission can affect the trial balance if the wrong account affects the balance.
distractorRationale.c: Errors of principle can affect the trial balance if they involve incorrect amounts.

questions.stem: A transaction was recorded as ₦3,000 instead of ₦30,000. What type of error is this?
questions.explanation: An error of original entry occurs when the wrong amount is recorded in the books.

distractorRationale.a: This is not an omission error since the transaction was recorded.
distractorRationale.b: This is not an error of commission as it was not recorded in the wrong account.
distractorRationale.c: This is not an error of principle as it does not violate accounting principles.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a suspense account?

options.text: To temporarily hold differences in the trial balance
To record all types of errors

questions.explanation: A suspense account is used to temporarily hold the difference when the trial balance does not agree.

distractorRationale.a: Suspense accounts are not for permanently holding transactions.
distractorRationale.c: Suspense accounts do not record errors but hold differences.
distractorRationale.d: Suspense accounts are not used directly for adjusting financial statements.

questions.explanation: Errors of principle do not always affect the trial balance; they affect the classification of accounts.

distractorRationale.a: Not all errors of principle affect the trial balance as they may involve correct amounts in wrong accounts.
